issues.legal_issue: Withdrawal of a suit to pursue a distinct statutory recovery process does not abandon the claim or bar that process.
material_facts: The creditor withdrew its money-recovery suit expressly to pursue a faster remedy under a statutory recovery scheme.
The statutory scheme preserved remedies available under other laws, and recovery by certificate followed a procedure distinct from a court suit.
The background showed that the creditor intended to continue recovery rather than abandon its claim.
issues.conclusion: The suit’s withdrawal did not abandon the claim and did not bar recovery under the statutory process.
issues.legal_principle: Order 23 Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure bars a fresh suit in the circumstances specified by the rule, but does not bar a distinct statutory recovery proceeding that is not a suit. Whether a claim was abandoned is a mixed question of law and fact, and the withdrawal order must be considered alongside the circumstances and the applicant’s intent. Sarguja Transport Service v. State Transport Appellate Tribunal cannot be applied without regard to the facts; Sarva Shramik Sanghatana v. State of Maharashtra and Ramesh Chandra Sankla v. Vikram Cement support examining the character and circumstances of the later proceeding. C.C.E. v. Ramdev Tobacco Company and ESI Corporation v. C.C. Santhakumar distinguish court proceedings from executive certificate recovery proceedings.

rule.if: statutory_recovery_proceeding and earlier_suit_withdrawn_to_pursue_recovery and recovery_process_is_distinct_from_a_suit and governing_scheme_preserves_other_remedies

predicates.statutory_recovery_proceeding: The creditor is pursuing recovery through a statutory certificate process rather than through a suit.
predicates.earlier_suit_withdrawn_to_pursue_recover: The creditor withdrew an earlier suit in order to pursue recovery through another process.
predicates.recovery_process_is_distinct_from_a_suit: The later recovery process is governed by a procedure distinct from proceedings in a court suit.
predicates.governing_scheme_preserves_other_remedie: The governing recovery scheme provides that its remedy does not displace remedies available under other laws.

issues.definition: When a creditor pursues a distinct statutory recovery process after withdrawing a suit to pursue that recovery, and the scheme preserves other remedies, the withdrawal does not bar the statutory process.

issues.legal_issue: Public policy and the doctrine of election do not prevent recovery of a loan merely because the creditor pursued one available recovery route after another.
material_facts: The loan was disbursed from public funds and only a small part was repaid.
The creditor pursued recovery through available legal processes, while the borrower repeatedly challenged or delayed those processes.
The governing scheme provided a recovery remedy without prejudice to other available remedies.
issues.conclusion: It would be contrary to public policy to prevent recovery of the loan, and reliance on the doctrine of election to bar recovery was misconceived.
issues.legal_principle: Public policy is a variable concept concerned with the larger interests of society, righteousness, good conscience, and equity; it cannot be invoked to help a borrower evade the obligation to repay a loan or to prevent lawful recovery. The court relied on P. Rathinam v. Union of India on the uncertain nature of public policy and on the recovery scheme’s preservation of other remedies. The doctrine of election did not apply on these facts.

rule.if: statutory_loan_recovery_case and loan_advanced_from_public_funds and borrower_repaid_only_a_small_part and creditor_pursued_lawful_recovery and recovery_remedies_are_cumulative

predicates.statutory_loan_recovery_case: The proceeding concerns recovery of a loan through a statutory recovery process.
predicates.loan_advanced_from_public_funds: The loan was advanced from funds held for public purposes.
predicates.borrower_repaid_only_a_small_part: The borrower repaid only a small part of the loan.
predicates.creditor_pursued_lawful_recovery: The creditor took steps through legal processes to recover the unpaid loan.
predicates.recovery_remedies_are_cumulative: The governing scheme allows its recovery remedy to coexist with other available remedies.

issues.definition: When a largely unpaid loan from public funds is pursued through lawful, cumulative recovery remedies, public policy and election do not bar recovery.

issues.legal_issue: Recovery is not time-barred where a recovery certificate had already been issued before the period of inaction relied on to find the claim barred.
material_facts: A recovery certificate for the industry loan had been issued before the period during which the High Court considered no recovery action had occurred.
The borrower challenged the certificate proceedings, and later proceedings followed after the earlier challenge was allowed on technical grounds with liberty to proceed afresh in accordance with law.
issues.conclusion: The finding that recovery of the industry loan was time-barred was factually erroneous; the recovery proceedings were not time-barred.
issues.legal_principle: The court rejected the limitation finding because its factual premise—that the creditor had taken no recovery action during the relevant interval—overlooked the earlier recovery certificate. The judgment does not identify a separate limitation provision or prescribe a general limitation period.

predicates.statutory_loan_recovery_challenge: The proceeding challenges recovery of a loan through a statutory process.
predicates.recovery_certificate_issued_before_alleg: A recovery certificate had been issued before the period said to show that the creditor took no action.
predicates.later_proceedings_followed_permission_to: Later recovery proceedings followed an earlier decision permitting the creditor to proceed afresh in accordance with law.

issues.definition: When a statutory loan recovery challenge relies on an alleged period of inactivity but a certificate had already been issued before that period, later proceedings following permission to proceed afresh are not time-barred on that basis.
